blocking.issue: Readiness gating (ADR-0015) is not achieved for traffic. The new process binds 8080, 8443 and 9901 with SO_REUSEPORT in step 3, before it warms and before the old process accepts it. From that bind on, the kernel spreads new connections across both sockets, so clients reach a process that has not passed its gate. If the handover is refused or times out, the new process exits and the connections queued on it are reset. That contradicts ZG-3 ('refuses no new TCP connection') and V-3 ('Zero refused connections'), and an operator cannot tell from the document whether a refused handover is safe. Acceptance criterion 6 fails on 'readiness gating'.
blocking.evidence: Line 174: "3. **Bind and gate.** It binds 8080, 8443 and 9901 with `SO_REUSEPORT` (in-flight QUIC on UDP 8443 is lost), warms, then reports version, format markers and active digest"; line 175: "A new process not accepted within 60 s (target) exits; the old one never started draining."; line 53: "ZG-3 | An in-place handover refuses no new TCP connection"
blocking.fix: State how new connections stay off the new sockets until acceptance. For example, the lock holder keeps an `SO_ATTACH_REUSEPORT_CBPF` program on each reuseport group that selects only its own socket, and step 5 swaps it for one that selects the new socket. Alternatively, the new process calls listen only after it is accepted. Reorder Figure 1 and steps 3 to 5 to match. Add a refused-handover case to V-3 with the pass criterion 'zero reset connections'.

blocking.section: Guarantees; Binary upgrades > Drain timeline defaults
blocking.issue: The document contradicts itself on readiness during a handover. ZG-3 and V-3 promise that /readyz stays at 200 throughout. The Drain timeline, however, applies to every Drain, including one started by an accepted handover, and its first row sets /readyz to 503 at 0 s. Figure 1 also has the old process 'fail readyz'. A balancer health check that reuses its connection to the old process sees 503 and marks the Node down. The document does not say which rule wins, so an operator cannot configure health checks for T5 or T2.
blocking.evidence: Line 186: "A Drain starts on SIGTERM, on `ruralz node drain` ... or on an accepted handover."; line 190: "| 0 s | Readiness failure: `/readyz` returns 503; heartbeats set `draining` | At once (target) |"; Figure 1: "Old->>Old: accept the queued connections, close listeners, fail readyz"; line 53: "keeps the Node's `/readyz` at 200 throughout"; line 389: "200 throughout a handover"
blocking.fix: Add a handover variant of the Drain timeline. In a handover, the old process closes its idle 9901 connections and answers in-flight admin requests with `Connection: close` after CBPF steers 9901, so every probe reaches the accepted new process, and it never serves a 503 /readyz on a kept-alive connection. Make the offsets explicit when no SIGTERM and no accept window occur, for example 'deadline 20 s after acceptance (target)'. Add a keep-alive health checker to V-3.

blocking.issue: The Kubernetes replacement cadence contradicts Deployment topologies, which this document depends on. That document sets the Node StatefulSet's RollingUpdate maxUnavailable to match the PodDisruptionBudget, which is one zone's share at minimum scale. This document says the update replaces one Pod at a time and sizes the headroom from that. An operator would get different upgrade durations and capacity loss depending on which document they follow.
blocking.evidence: Line 132: "| Replacement | Kubernetes (T4) | StatefulSet rolling update: preStop, Drain, new Pod | One Pod at a time, within the PodDisruptionBudget |"; line 251: "Each step removes one Pod for about 40 to 45 s (hypothesis), so `minReplicas` SHOULD hold one zone's share of headroom." Deployment topologies: "| Node StatefulSet | `podManagementPolicy: Parallel` ...; `RollingUpdate`, `maxUnavailable` matching the PodDisruptionBudget" and "| PodDisruptionBudgets | One `ruralz-control` pod; for Nodes, one zone's share at minimum scale (target) |"
blocking.fix: Change the Capacity cell to "Up to `maxUnavailable` Pods at a time, equal to the PodDisruptionBudget (one zone's share at minimum scale, target), per Deployment topologies". Restate line 251 so that each step removes up to one zone's share for about 40 to 45 s (hypothesis). Note that the PodDisruptionBudget limits evictions, not the StatefulSet controller's own rolling update.

blocking.issue: ZG-1, the first guarantee operators read, misstates the retirement behavior that the document's own Atomic swap paragraph and Data plane define. Streams pinned to the oldest retired snapshot are closed at once when a third retirement occurs. They get no 30 s grace; only whatever is still pinned after the grace ends with RZ-RT-014. An operator planning frequent Hot Reloads would underestimate how many WebSocket, gRPC and SSE streams are closed.
blocking.evidence: Line 51: "ZG-1 | A Hot Reload drops no in-flight request; only a stream that outlives K + 1 further activations and a 30 s grace ends, K = 2 (target)"; line 88: "a third retirement closes the oldest one's streams (WebSocket 1001, gRPC `UNAVAILABLE`, SSE end with a retry hint) and ends the rest after a 30 s grace (target) with `RZ-RT-014`"
blocking.fix: Reword ZG-1: "A Hot Reload drops no in-flight request. When a third snapshot retires, streams pinned to the oldest receive a going-away close at once, and anything still pinned 30 s later (target) ends with RZ-RT-014; K = 2 (target)."
